description: The hand-verified expected outcome for oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/unknown-shape.json -- the shape layer's fall-through case. It states a HALT, not rows, despite the .rows.json suffix this folder's naming convention requires: the suffix names the folder's contract (one expected file per fixture), not the shape of every outcome. Every value was derived by reading the fixture and the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/shape.py and harness/lib/normalize/paths.py; each derivation is written out field by field below so a reader can check it without running anything, and execution was used only to corroborate a derivation already written, never as its source. Where this file and shape.py disagree, the disagreement is the finding: diagnose it rather than overwriting this file to match.
null_field_note: tool, scanner_class, adapter and adapter_invoked are null rather than omitted, so a generic loader reads this file with the same keys as the positive expected files in this folder. They are null because the halt precedes tool resolution: a document whose name resolves to no canonical tool has no tool, therefore no scanner_class from the class table and no adapter to route to -- and therefore no adapter whose invocation status could be true or false. The categorical statement that nothing was invoked is carried as a boolean in adapter_invocation.any_adapter_invoked, not by overloading a null here.

fixture.authored_note: An authored generic report, not captured tool output. It is none of the nine runner artifacts and imitates none of them: no version/runs pair (SARIF), no top-level array (gitleaks), no Results (trivy), no results.failed_checks in either form (checkov), no dependencies (dependency-check), no findings/queries pair (joern) and no results[].packages[].vulnerabilities[] (osv-scanner). Nothing in it is a finding, a secret, a credential or a token.
fixture.example_location_note: The fixture's single observations entry names core/src/main/scala/org/apache/spark/storage/DiskStore.scala line 72 -- the in-scope Spark location this harness uses as its example throughout -- so the fixture invents no path. It stays an example coordinate inside a document that never reaches an adapter: no path is resolved from it, no row carries it, and naming it here characterises nothing about that file.
fixture.keys_are_recorded_exhaustively: All seven top-level keys are listed above in document order, and near_miss_keys below carries one entry per key. So this file's account of the fixture is checkable in both directions -- nothing recorded here is absent from the fixture, and nothing in the fixture's top level is unaccounted for.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant. Recorded for parity with the positive expected files in this folder; no row below carries it, because rows is empty by expectation.

shape_detection.conjunction: isinstance(doc, Mapping) and doc.get("version") == "2.1.0" and isinstance(doc.get("runs"), list)
shape_detection.conjunction_authority: AAP 0.5.4: an artifact is SARIF when it carries version "2.1.0" together with a runs array -- those two together are the test.
shape_detection.version_observed_note: null because the key is ABSENT, not because it carries JSON null. shape.describe_document reports the observed version as doc.get("version"), which is None either way, so the absence itself is recorded separately in version_key_present rather than inferred from this value.
shape_detection.runs_observed_json_type_note: shape.detection_evidence names the JSON type of doc.get("runs"). The key is absent, so that value is None and its type reads "null" rather than "absent". Recorded verbatim so a reader comparing this file against the evidence record in harness/artifacts/logs/normalize-run.json is not surprised by it.
shape_detection.is_sarif_derivation: The document is a mapping, so the first condition holds. It carries no version key, so doc.get("version") is None and None == "2.1.0" is False. It carries no runs key, so doc.get("runs") is None and isinstance(None, list) is False. BOTH halves of the conjunction fail.
shape_detection.distinct_from_the_near_sarif_twins: near-sarif-version-only.json and near-sarif-runs-only.json each fail exactly ONE half, which is what makes them the pair that pins the conjunction. This fixture fails both halves and every native signature as well, so it is not a probe of the conjunction: it is the fall-through, the case where nothing matches anything. The three are complementary and none substitutes for another.
shape_detection.membership_test_note: No relaxation of the test accepts this document either. It carries no version key at all, so a prefix compare, a parsed-version compare or a truthiness test on version has nothing to read; it carries no runs key, so "runs" in doc and bool(doc.get("runs")) are both False. The keys it does carry are near misses only in the eye of a substring or fuzzy matcher, which is what near_miss_keys below pins.
shape_detection.sarif_adapter_invoked_basis: Two independent reasons, either sufficient. First, is_sarif is False, so normalize.shape.route never selects SHARED_SARIF_ADAPTER on the SARIF branch. Second, and decisive for this fixture, route raises before any adapter is selected at all, because the fixture's filename resolves to no canonical tool -- so no adapter module is named and none is imported or called.
shape_detection.counterfactual_note: Recorded so the guarantee is not overclaimed. Routing is keyed by the writing runner's artifact filename, never sniffed from content, and a KNOWN name never halts in this module -- an adapter owns its own structural validation. So had this document been presented under one of the nine names it would not halt here: it would route with shape "native" -- never "sarif", since is_sarif is False -- to that runner's adapter, which would then reject or halt on its own terms. The invariants this fixture pins are therefore the three that hold under its own name: the halt is raised, it is the NAMED halt, and no adapter is reached at all.

native_shape_detection.checks_note: The document's seven top-level keys are report_format, format_revision, generated_at, producer, Result, findings_summary and observations. There is no results key at all, so neither Checkov's results.failed_checks nor OSV-Scanner's results[].packages[].vulnerabilities[] can exist; there is no Results, no dependencies, and no findings/queries pair; and the top level is an object, so the gitleaks array form and Checkov's multi-framework array form are both excluded by type before any key is read.
native_shape_detection.detection_mechanism_note: Recorded so these verdicts are not mistaken for a description of shape.py's control flow. shape.py performs NO content-based native detection: a document is SARIF or it is "the native adapter keyed by the runner that wrote it" (AAP 0.5.4), and the writer is identified by the artifact's filename. The verdicts above are therefore the signatures a content-sniffing implementation would key on, each recorded False so that (a) no such implementation could route this document anywhere, and (b) the fuzzy variants named in near_miss_keys are pinned as wrong. They are evidence about the document, not a claim that shape.py evaluates them.
native_shape_detection.name_resolution_authority: normalize.shape.resolve_tool over the authored tables CANONICAL_TOOLS and ARTIFACT_FILENAME_BY_TOOL in harness/lib/normalize/shape.py. The nine canonical identifiers and nine artifact filenames are not copied here -- shape.py is the single authority, exactly as harness/scope/allowlist.txt is the single authority for the scope globs.
native_shape_detection.name_resolution_note: "unknown-shape.json" is not one of the nine artifact filenames and not one of the nine canonical tool identifiers, so resolve_tool returns None. Matching there is exact and case-sensitive, so no near spelling resolves either.

container_check.note: The top level is a JSON object, which IS a container an adapter could own, so the second halt reason shape.py names -- REASON_UNSUPPORTED_DOCUMENT_TYPE, for a top level that is neither a JSON object nor a JSON array -- does not apply. That is deliberate: this fixture must halt for being unrecognisable, not for being structurally impossible, and a fixture that halted on the container check would leave the fall-through path untested.

near_miss_keys.would_be_read_as: a format or version declaration standing in for SARIF's version
near_miss_keys.matcher_that_would_wrongly_accept: a detector accepting any format-or-version-shaped key rather than the exact key "version"
near_miss_keys.why_it_does_not_match: The SARIF test reads exactly the key "version" and compares it to exactly the string "2.1.0". A different key name is not that key, however similar its role.

near_miss_keys.would_be_read_as: a version number, satisfying the version half of the SARIF conjunction
near_miss_keys.matcher_that_would_wrongly_accept: a detector that parses or coerces a version rather than comparing the exact string, or that treats any *_revision / *_version key as the version
near_miss_keys.why_it_does_not_match: The key is not "version", and the value is a JSON number rather than the string "2.1.0". shape.py compares the exact string precisely so that "2.1", "2.1.0-rc" and a numeric revision are all rejected.

near_miss_keys.would_be_read_as: nothing -- no detector in the contract keys on a timestamp
near_miss_keys.why_it_does_not_match: Recorded for exhaustiveness rather than as a near miss: it appears in no signature, so no matcher keys on it. Listing it keeps this file's account of the fixture's top level complete in both directions.

near_miss_keys.would_be_read_as: producer provenance, standing in for SARIF's runs[].tool.driver or for the joern envelope's tool/tool_version pair
near_miss_keys.matcher_that_would_wrongly_accept: a detector treating provenance as a shape test -- keying on a tool/driver/producer identity instead of on the conjunction
near_miss_keys.why_it_does_not_match: shape.py's docstring states the exclusion directly: $schema, a .sarif extension and a tool.driver key are NOT substitutes for the two conditions. Provenance names who wrote a document; it does not establish what shape the document is.

near_miss_keys.matcher_that_would_wrongly_accept: a substring, prefix or case-insensitive key match -- "Result" in key, key.startswith("Result"), key.lower() == "results" -- or a truthiness test on the value
near_miss_keys.why_it_does_not_match: Trivy's signature is a top-level Results key holding an ARRAY. This key differs in name (singular, no trailing s) and in type (a string), so an exact-key-plus-type test rejects it twice over. This is the strengthening the fixture exists for: a fuzzy matcher accepts it and then finds nothing iterable inside.

near_miss_keys.matcher_that_would_wrongly_accept: a prefix or substring key match -- key.startswith("findings"), "findings" in key -- or a detector satisfied by one half of the joern findings/queries pair
near_miss_keys.why_it_does_not_match: The joern envelope's signature is a findings ARRAY together with a queries array. This key is neither of those names, its value is an object rather than an array, and no queries key exists anywhere in the document, so both halves of that pair fail as well.

near_miss_keys.value_summary: one finding-shaped element: an identifier, a label, a band and a location with a file and a line
near_miss_keys.would_be_read_as: a records array -- SARIF's runs[].results[], gitleaks' top-level array, or Checkov's results.failed_checks
near_miss_keys.matcher_that_would_wrongly_accept: a detector that sniffs content for the first array of finding-shaped objects instead of reading the writer's name and the two SARIF conditions
near_miss_keys.why_it_does_not_match: It is not a top-level array (the document is an object), it is not named by any signature in the contract, and no adapter's count unit points at it. It is the most dangerous key in the fixture precisely because a content-sniffing detector could map it to one plausible-looking row -- which is the silent wrong answer this halt exists to prevent.

near_miss_keys_note: One entry per top-level key the fixture carries, in document order, so the list is exhaustive against the fixture rather than a selection: every key recorded here is present in the fixture and every key the fixture's top level carries is recorded here. Two are the near misses the fixture was strengthened with -- "Result" for Trivy's Results and "findings_summary" for the joern envelope's findings -- and none of the seven may cause a match.
fuzzy_matching_requirement: Every must_match above is false, and a detector that accepts any one of them is defective. The failure is silent rather than loud in every case: a fuzzy match on "Result" or "findings_summary" finds nothing iterable and reports zero rows, and a content sniff on "observations" reports one plausible row from a document no runner wrote. Both outcomes are indistinguishable from a real result, which is why the requirement is a halt and why exact key names and exact types are the whole of the test.

named_halt_requirement.statement: A KeyError or a TypeError escaping a half-attempted parse is a FAILURE, not a pass. The requirement is the named halt, not merely that something was raised. An implementation that reaches into the document -- doc["version"], doc["runs"][0], iterating a value it assumed was a list -- and blows up part-way through has produced an accident that happens to stop the run, not a decision to stop it: it has no reason attribute, it names no artifact, it quotes no observed structure, it cannot be told apart from a defect in the normalizer itself, and the same code path against a slightly different unrecognised document might not raise at all.
named_halt_requirement.why_this_is_the_most_important_expectati: Every other expectation in this file describes a value; this one describes the difference between a designed outcome and a coincidence. The halt is only useful if it is reliable and self-describing, and only a deliberate raise can be either. AAP 0.5.4 requires a halt rather than a best-effort parse, and AAP 0.9.2 lists an artifact matching neither SARIF nor a known native shape among the conditions that stop the run -- neither is satisfied by an incidental exception from a parse that was attempted anyway.
named_halt_requirement.assertion_form: The test must name shape.UnknownArtifactShape. Naming it is already sufficient to exclude the two forbidden types -- neither KeyError nor TypeError is a subclass of it, and it is a subclass of neither, so an isinstance check against it rejects both -- while an assertion written against Exception or BaseException, or a bare try/except that only records that something was raised, passes on exactly the failure this expectation forbids. Asserting the exact type is stricter still and is what oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/test_shape_routing_negative.py is expected to do.
named_halt_requirement.raised_by_the_shape_layer: The exception must come from normalize.shape.route or normalize.shape.route_artifact -- the module that owns the decision -- rather than be constructed by a caller after the fact. A halt synthesised outside the shape layer would leave the shape layer's own fall-through path untested.

halt.exception_relationship_to_forbidden_type: UnknownArtifactShape derives directly from Exception. KeyError (via LookupError) and TypeError derive from Exception independently, so neither is a subclass of UnknownArtifactShape and UnknownArtifactShape is a subclass of neither. The three are mutually exclusive under isinstance, which is what makes the named assertion in named_halt_requirement.assertion_form sufficient.
halt.raised_before: any adapter module is named, imported or called, and before any record traversal of any kind
halt.reason_note: shape.py names two reasons. This document's top level is a JSON object, which is a supported container, so REASON_UNSUPPORTED_DOCUMENT_TYPE does not apply; the halt is attributed to the name that resolves to no tool. Both facts matter: the reason must be the name reason, and it must not be the container reason.

observed_attributes.artifact_path_note: Whatever subject the caller passed, echoed unchanged -- route never rewrites it. The value above is the repository-relative fixture path the negative test passes; no absolute path appears anywhere in this file.
observed_attributes.stem_note: shape._artifact_name returns PurePath(text).name, so this attribute carries the filename component including its extension rather than a suffix-stripped stem.

halt.observed_attributes_note: These are the attributes the halt carries so a report can quote the observed structure without re-reading the artifact. They are the reason a deliberate raise is required rather than an incidental one: an escaping KeyError carries none of them.
halt.details_method: shape.UnknownArtifactShape.details() returns the same facts as a flat JSON-serialisable mapping, adding expected_artifacts -- the nine artifact filenames, taken from shape.ARTIFACT_FILENAMES rather than copied here, so the one authority cannot drift into two.
halt.sarif_detected_note: False, which is what distinguishes this halt from the other failure UnknownArtifactShape reports: a document that IS valid SARIF appearing under a name harness/artifacts/raw/ must never contain. This document is not SARIF under any relaxation of the test, so no such message applies.
halt.authority: AAP 0.5.4 -- an artifact matching neither the SARIF shape nor a known native shape is a halt rather than a best-effort parse -- and AAP 0.9.2, which lists it among the conditions that stop the run.

not_a_rejection.reject_classes_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, the REJECT_CLASSES tuple -- a closed set of ten class names, not copied here so the one authority cannot drift into two.
not_a_rejection.statement: The stated outcome is a halt, not a counted rejection: "halt", "UnknownArtifactShape" and "unrecognized-artifact-name" are each provably absent from paths.REJECT_CLASSES, and the test asserts that non-membership programmatically rather than by inspection. A rejection is a per-record outcome inside an adapter that already owns the artifact; this document never reaches an adapter, so there is no record to reject and nothing to count under any class.

parse.note: The fixture is well-formed JSON and json.load succeeds on it. No parser failure is expected here and none is stated: malformed input is a different condition, owned by the reject-*-malformed-record fixtures, and conflating the two would let a JSON syntax error pass as a shape halt.
parse.why_well_formedness_is_the_point: A document that fails to parse is stopped by the parser, and no shape decision is ever reached -- so a malformed fixture could not exercise this path at all. It is precisely a document that parses perfectly and is still unrecognisable that tempts a best-effort parse: everything is readable, the keys look plausible, one array even looks like findings, and reading it "as far as it goes" feels like the helpful thing to do. That temptation is what the named halt refuses, and only a well-formed fixture puts it in front of the implementation.

boundaries.malformed_input: owned by the reject-*-malformed-record fixtures in this folder -- a different condition, counted as a rejection class rather than raised as a shape halt
boundaries.one_half_of_the_sarif_conjunction: owned by oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/near-sarif-version-only.json and oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/near-sarif-runs-only.json, which fail one condition each
boundaries.a_recognised_artifact_that_is_structural: owned by the adapter, not by this layer -- oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/halt-trivy-unsupported-section.json is the folder's instance, and shape.py deliberately does not pre-empt an adapter's validation
boundaries.this_fixture: the fall-through: well-formed, unrecognisable, and matching nothing under any detector

why_this_case_is_real.statement: Nine independent runners populate harness/artifacts/raw/, each writing its own artifact in its own format on its own schedule, and the normalizer walks that directory rather than a hand-picked list. Something unexpected landing there is therefore an operational possibility rather than a hypothetical -- a renamed or partially written artifact, a file left by a tool upgrade, an output form a runner produced under a condition nobody anticipated, or a stray file copied in by hand.
why_this_case_is_real.consequence: Because the input is a directory this run does not fully control, the fall-through is a path the normalizer will one day take. What it does then must be a deliberate, named halt with the observed structure quoted -- not whatever exception happens to surface first from a parse that was attempted anyway, and not a best-effort read that emits some rows and reports success.
why_this_case_is_real.raw_tree_contract: harness/artifacts/raw/ is runner-only: one artifact per tool that writes one and nothing else ever (AAP 0.6.1). This expectation is what makes that contract enforceable rather than merely stated -- an artifact that does not belong stops the run instead of quietly entering the dataset.
why_this_case_is_real.no_interpretation: Recording that nine runners write there is a statement about how the directory is populated. It compares no tool against another, ranks nothing and characterises no tool's output.

adapter_invocation.adapter_modules_authority: shape.ADAPTER_MODULES in harness/lib/normalize/shape.py -- the distinct adapter module keys serving the nine tools. Not copied here, so the routing table has one authority.
adapter_invocation.statement: No adapter was invoked. route raises before an adapter is selected, so no adapter module is named, none is imported and none is called -- not the shared SARIF adapter and not any of the per-tool native adapters. Nothing inside the document is read beyond its top level: no field is mapped, no severity is mapped, no path is resolved and no in_scope predicate is evaluated.
adapter_invocation.verifiability: shape.py imports no adapter module at all -- routing names an adapter by string key and cli.py resolves the key to a callable -- so the negative test can assert this without importing any adapter, and an adapter cannot have run as a side effect of the routing call.

counts.reconciliation_identity: not applicable -- the halt precedes any record traversal, so no count unit exists to reconcile against

counts_note: raw_finding_records and raw_count_unit are null rather than 0. A count unit is a property of an artifact's known shape -- runs[].results[] for SARIF, Results[].Vulnerabilities[] and its siblings for Trivy -- and this document has no known shape, so there is no unit for normalize.reconcile.count_records to walk. Writing 0 there would assert that a traversal ran and found nothing, which is precisely the empty-result-set reading this fixture exists to prevent; writing 1 -- the length of the fixture's observations array -- would be worse still, since choosing that array as the count unit IS the content sniff the near-miss keys forbid. rows and rejections are 0 because nothing was emitted and nothing was rejected.
rows_note: Explicitly empty, and empty for a different reason than a clean scan is empty: the pipeline stopped, it did not look and find nothing. The distinction is measurable here rather than rhetorical -- the fixture carries one finding-shaped element, so a row count of 1 would expose a content-sniffing detector and a row count of 0 reported alongside a successful parse status would expose a permissive one. Only 0 rows together with the named halt is the expected outcome.
row_derivations_note: Empty because no row exists to derive. The positive expected files in this folder carry one derivation per row, field by field; there is nothing here for that section to describe.
guarded_failure: A permissive detector that accepts an unrecognisable document does not raise -- it produces an EMPTY RESULT SET, and an empty result set is indistinguishable from a clean scan (AAP 0.5.4). This fixture makes both failure modes concrete. A detector that reached the shared SARIF adapter with this document would look for runs, find nothing, and report success with zero rows. A detector that fuzzy-matched "Result" or "findings_summary" would select a section that holds no records and report the same zero. A detector that sniffed for the first finding-shaped array would emit one row from a document no runner wrote. All three report success; none reports a problem. The required outcome is the named halt, never a silent zero and never a plausible one.

assertions: normalize.shape.route_artifact over this fixture's path and its parsed document raises shape.UnknownArtifactShape.

The raised type is that exception rather than a bare KeyError or TypeError: the assertion names shape.UnknownArtifactShape, and asserting the exact type is stricter and preferred. An assertion written against Exception or BaseException does not satisfy this.
exc.reason equals shape.REASON_UNRECOGNIZED_ARTIFACT_NAME and is not shape.REASON_UNSUPPORTED_DOCUMENT_TYPE.
exc.sarif_detected is False, and the halt's observed attributes carry the top-level type, the observed version, the top-level keys and the length recorded above.
shape.is_sarif over the parsed document is False, and every native signature in native_shape_detection.checks is False -- including the two near-miss keys, which must not cause a match.
No adapter is invoked: the routing call names, imports and calls no adapter module.
The rows array is empty and the rejection total is 0.
Neither the outcome nor the halt reason is a member of paths.REJECT_CLASSES, asserted programmatically over that tuple rather than by inspection.
json.load over the fixture succeeds -- well-formedness is asserted, not assumed, since a fixture that stopped parsing would exercise none of the above.
The near-miss keys recorded in this file are exactly the fixture's top-level keys, so this expectation cannot drift from the fixture it describes.
negative_test_contract.mandated_direction_note: AAP 0.5.4 mandates a negative test asserting that a NATIVE artifact does not route to the SARIF adapter; that assertion is owned by the same test file over the native fixtures. This fixture extends it to the fall-through -- a document that is neither SARIF nor any known native shape -- which is the case the mandated direction leaves untested.

related_fixtures.near_sarif_pair_role: Each fails exactly one half of the SARIF conjunction, so together they pin the conjunction. They share this fixture's expected outcome -- is_sarif False, no adapter invoked, zero rows, zero rejections, a shape.UnknownArtifactShape halt -- and differ in that they are near misses of one test while this fixture matches nothing at all.
related_fixtures.malformed_record_fixtures: the reject-*-malformed-record fixtures in this folder, which own malformed and wrongly-shaped input as counted rejection classes inside an adapter that already owns its artifact
related_fixtures.adapter_owned_halt: oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/halt-trivy-unsupported-section.json -- a halt raised by an adapter under a recognised name, which is the boundary shape.py deliberately does not cross
related_fixtures.note: Named so a reader can see which layer owns which failure. No fixture's outcome is inferred from another's, and each expected file states its own.

behaviours_not_exercised_by_this_fixture: Row construction of any kind -- no adapter runs, so no field mapping, no severity mapping and no in_scope evaluation is exercised.

Path resolution -- normalize.paths is never called, so no path base, no uriBaseId walk and no non-filesystem coordinate serialisation is exercised, and the example location the fixture names is never resolved.
Per-record rejection -- none of the ten classes in paths.REJECT_CLASSES is reachable from a shape halt.
The other halt reason in shape.py, REASON_UNSUPPORTED_DOCUMENT_TYPE, which needs a top level that is neither a JSON object nor a JSON array; this document's top level is an object.
The valid-SARIF-under-an-unexpected-name halt, whose sarif_detected attribute is True; this document's is False.
One half of the SARIF conjunction holding while the other fails, which the near-SARIF pair owns; both halves fail here.
An adapter's own structural validation and its own halt, which a recognised artifact name reaches and an unrecognised one never does.
Malformed JSON, owned by the reject-*-malformed-record fixtures.
The reconciliation identity, which has no raw finding record count to assert over here.
how_to_check_this_file: Parse the fixture, compare its sha256 and byte size against the fixture block, and confirm its top-level keys equal the keys listed there and in near_miss_keys. Read shape.py and confirm UnknownArtifactShape is defined there with Exception as its base and is raised by route and route_artifact for a name that resolves to no tool. Read paths.py and confirm REJECT_CLASSES holds ten names, none of them the outcome, the exception or the reason recorded here. Then run the negative test: every assertion in negative_test_contract is checkable from this file alone.
prohibitions_observed: No secret value, credential, token or redacted-secret placeholder appears in any field of this file (the tree is committed to git). No finding is judged -- nothing here is called real, important, a false positive or a duplicate. Nothing is deduplicated. No tool's output is characterised against another's: this file describes one document's shape detection and the halt it must produce, and nothing else.

under_each_recognised_name.envelope: a SARIF 2.1.0 document -- version == "2.1.0" together with a runs array; this runner writes SARIF and nothing else, so there is no native shape to fall back to
a SARIF 2.1.0 document -- version == "2.1.0" together with a runs array; this runner writes SARIF and nothing else, so there is no native shape to fall back to

either one report object carrying a 'results' object, or a non-empty top-level array of such report objects (the multi-framework form)

under_each_recognised_name_note: Nine entries, one per artifact filename, in canonical tool order, recording what routing does with THIS document under a name that does resolve. Every outcome is a halt, and the reason splits by whether the name belongs to a SARIF producer: those three runners write SARIF and nothing else, so their artifact failing the conjunction is a producer-or-version condition, while any other recognised name over an unrecognised envelope is a mis-written or mis-placed artifact. The table is derived from shape._NATIVE_ENVELOPE and asserted against shape.route, so the record and the router cannot drift apart.
